validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: strongly confirmed, real, correctly classified. This is Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company's FERC-certificated '2017 Expansion Project' (Docket No. CP17-28-000, pre-filing PF16-7-000), an interstate transmission expansion under FERC jurisdiction -- not a phantom or GEM-only entity. Verified directly against: (1) the FERC Environmental Assessment for the docket (295pp, downloaded via Wayback since the live ferc.gov path 404s -- URL rot, not a deletion; the doc itself explicitly names '2017 Expansion Project' and Docket CP17-28-000 on every page), which states Eastern Shore requests authorization for 'approximately 40 miles of pipeline...located in Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Delaware' comprising 22.7 mi of 10/16/24-inch loop + a 16.9-mi 10-inch mainline extension + Daleville compressor upgrade + Honey Brook meter/regulator upgrade + two DE pressure control stations, for 61,162 Dth/d of additional firm capacity; (2) Chesapeake Utilities Corp's SEC 10-K filings for FY2017 and FY2018 (Eastern Shore's parent, publicly traded NYSE:CPK), which independently describe the identical project scope, confirm FERC issued the CP in October 2017, the first phase (TETLP interconnect) went into service December 2017, and by 12/31/2018 the project was 'substantially completed' with remaining segments finishing in 2019; (3) two Natural Gas Intelligence articles (Jan 2017 filing news, Oct 2017 certificate-issued news) independently corroborating docket number, capacity, mileage breakdown (22.7 + 16.9 mi), and operator identity; (4) Eastern Shore's own current project page (esng.com/project/2017-expansion/), which gives the full month-by-month in-service schedule Dec 2017 through Sept 2019. All four sources agree on scope and identity -- this is not a duplicate of, or confusable with, sibling Eastern Shore rows P0182 (the 732-mi legacy main line, in service since 1959) or P6003 (Del-Mar Energy Pathway, a distinct 2019-filed, ~19-mi DE/MD project under Docket CP18-548-000) -- the three are genuinely distinct phases/projects of one system, consistent with the batch's own framing. Opened 6 of this row's 11 harvested wiki citations (esng.com project page, FERC EA, both NGI articles, esng.com home implicit via project page, and -- reached from the harvested PR Newswire citation for the sibling Del-Mar project -- Chesapeake's own press release, which also states Eastern Shore's total system is 486 route-miles, see cross_row_leads); did not separately open the EIA aggregate data-portal page or the FracTracker national map (both are system/national-level aggregates, not segment-specific refs per the aggregate-vs-segment rule) or the abarrelfull.wikidot.com citation (banned source, standing rule 5, not opened for citation purposes). One genuine spec concern surfaced -- see the second validity record below (SegmentCost).

validity.recommendation: revise SegmentCost to Chesapeake Utilities' own $117.0M estimate, or at minimum flag the $99M figure as unconfirmed against the operator's SEC disclosure
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current SegmentCost = $99,000,000 matches Natural Gas Intelligence's Oct. 5, 2017 article ('The expansion, estimated to cost around $99 million'), which is a genuine independent trade-press source and is presumably where the $99M figure in GEM originated. BUT the project's own owner/operator states a materially different, higher figure in a legally-filed SEC disclosure: Chesapeake Utilities Corporation's FY2017 Form 10-K (filed 2018-03-01, SEC EDGAR accession 0001628280-18-002594) states twice, in two separate sections (MD&A and the notes to financial statements): 'We expect to invest approximately $117.0 million in this expansion project' and 'The estimated cost of the 2017 Expansion Project is approximately $117.0 million.' The company's current live project page (esng.com/project/2017-expansion/) independently repeats the same figure: '$117 Million Capital Investment.' The 10-K and the current esng.com page are not independent of each other (same corporate origin), but the 10-K is a primary, SEC-filed, legally significant disclosure of the company's own cost estimate for this specific project -- a stronger origin than a trade-press 'estimated to cost around' figure. $99M vs $117M is an ~18% gap, which is material. I could not find a source stating a final/actual (as opposed to estimated) capitalized cost that reconciles the two. Did not find corroboration of the $99M NGI figure beyond that one article. Recommend either revising SegmentCost to 117000000 (sourced to the company's own 10-K) or, at minimum, not treating the current $99M value as confirmed -- do not add the NGI URL as a confirming ref for the sheet's current number without flagging this conflict.

cross_row_leads.facts: May 2019 Chesapeake Utilities/PR Newswire release states: 'Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company, a subsidiary of Chesapeake Utilities Corporation, owns and operates a 486-mile interstate pipeline that transports natural gas from various points in Pennsylvania to customers in Delaware, Maryland and Pennsylvania.' This directly disputes P0182's LengthKnown=732 mi for the Eastern Shore main line -- a 486-mile total system figure from the parent company's own press material.

Oct. 5, 2017 NGI article independently states: 'Eastern Shore operates a roughly 500-mile pipeline system that interconnects in Pennsylvania with Transco, Tetco and Columbia Gas Transmission LLC and extends through Delaware and into Maryland.' A second, independent (trade-press) source giving a total-system figure in the 486-500 mi range, corroborating the PR Newswire figure above and jointly contradicting P0182's 732 mi.

Del-Mar Energy Pathway Project (Docket No. CP18-548-000, applied for Sept. 2018): ~12 mi of new pipeline in Kent & Sussex Counties, DE plus ~7 mi in Wicomico & Somerset Counties, MD (~19 mi total, close to GEM's P6003 LengthKnown=20.0 mi); 11.8 MMcf/d additional firm + 2.5 MMcf/d off-peak transportation service (~14.3 MMcf/d combined, close to GEM's P6003 Capacity=14.00 MMcf/d); projected cost approximately $37 million; FERC certificate anticipated Q2/Q3 2019, construction expected to commence later in 2019.

summary: P2003 (Eastern Shore 2017 Expansion) is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate -- existence/scope strongly confirmed against the FERC EA, both Chesapeake Utilities 10-Ks, two NGI articles and esng.com (length, diameter, capacity, dates, operator, owner all corroborated at high tier); one spec concern staged: SegmentCost's current $99M (NGI-sourced) conflicts with the operator's own SEC 10-K and current project page, both stating $117.0M. UNRESOLVED: Pressure and FuelSource (no citable source found for either).
